citations.description: Test labeled 'RED-first' only runs the fixed gate; no pre-fix snapshot is loaded or invoked.

findings.criterion: A RED-first test proves the OLD gate passes a synthetic inert field whose name is reused on an unrelated config, and that the fixed gate fails it. Run both versions in-process from a snapshot COPY of the pre-fix script -- never `git stash`, which is global across all worktrees sharing this host's git common dir.
findings.detail: The test `test_same_named_field_on_an_unrelated_config_does_not_satisfy_it` (labeled 'Bug 2c58 (RED-first)') only runs the FIXED gate and asserts it fires on `CodeHealthConfig.enabled`. It does not run the OLD gate from a snapshot copy of the pre-fix script. No snapshot copy of the pre-fix script exists anywhere in the repository (searched for `check_config_reads_pre_fix`, `check_config_reads_old`, `check_config_reads_snapshot`, `pre_fix_gate`, `old_gate`, `field_name in reads` — all returned no matches). The AC explicitly requires running both versions in-process from a snapshot copy.

citations.description: The check() function has no ticket-id marker detection logic.
No test in the heldout suite covers ticket-id marker reporting.

findings.criterion: Any `# read-via:` marker whose pointer names a rebar ticket id is reported (design step 4); today that list is empty.
findings.detail: The script `scripts/check_config_reads.py` has no logic to detect or report `# read-via:` markers whose pointer names a rebar ticket id. The `check()` function only validates that a marker has a non-empty pointer; it does not scan for ticket-id patterns. No test in either gate test file covers this functionality. The design step 4 ('report any existing `# read-via:` marker whose pointer names a rebar ticket id') is absent from the implementation.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: for each one, decide whether the work is genuinely incomplete or simply undocumented. If a requirement is already satisfied but the proof is not discoverable from the code alone, add a comment to this ticket that documents the evidence — cite the concrete artifacts that meet the requirement (file paths and line ranges, commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the work to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. For any criterion whose work is genuinely unfinished, complete it, then re-verify.
